name: Deployment Plan
one_liner: How the solution reaches production, is validated there, and is watched.
purpose: The Deployment Plan defines the strategy, the roles and responsibilities and the tasks needed to ensure the information system can be deployed, run and managed by the IT operations team. Because it focuses on the technical aspects of deployment it is closely related to IT operations concerns such as cut-over, rollbacks and back-out procedures for contingency and risk management. It must have enough detail for operations to deploy, run and manage the system, and it is complemented — not replaced — by the PM² Transition Plan and Business Implementation Plan, which cover the client organisation's readiness.

fields.what: The strategy applied for the deployment efforts during the project lifecycle, outlined and communicated to everyone involved.
fields.pollux: Continuous delivery to pre-production; a scheduled cut-over window per quarterly release.

fields.what: Who does what in a deployment — creating consensus and awareness of the efforts involved in a successful technical deployment.
fields.pollux: Operations executes the production cut-over; the team supplies the package and the smoke-test list.

fields.what: The tasks that must be taken into account so the system can be deployed, run and managed by IT operations.
fields.pollux: Pre-load freeze, package deploy, configuration apply, smoke tests, access re-enable.

fields.what: Details the complete deployment process: features becoming available, work packages, libraries, environment requirements, generated configuration data.
fields.pollux: Release 2 deploys three units — data layer, API with reconciliation, portal UI.

fields.what: The mechanisms guaranteeing the deployment was done correctly — stress and performance tests, smoke tests on key features.
fields.pollux: Smoke test: one member state's total must match last night's reconciled control figure.

fields.what: Validation may show a correction is required, possibly resulting in a full roll-back of the deployment.
fields.pollux: Roll-back window of ninety minutes; Release 2 used it once during a rehearsal.

fields.what: Foreseen mechanisms to detect, report and solve problems, identifying potential issues before they become real problems.
fields.pollux: Load-completion alert before 06:00 CET; failure pages the on-call data engineer.

fields.what: Closely related to IT operations: cut-over, rollbacks and back-out procedures for contingency and risk management.
fields.pollux: Cut-over on the Thursday evening before each release date, back-out decision by 22:00.

fields.what: Closely related: both artefacts are vital to ensure the system can be deployed and used in production environments.
fields.who: ArOw owns the model · TeCo the plan
fields.pollux: Deployment units in the plan are exactly the three units named in the Operational Model.

fields.what: The PM² Transition Plan and Business Implementation Plan complement it by covering client readiness — training, support.
fields.pollux: National-authority training sits in the Business Implementation Plan, not here.

fields.what: Must consider the iterative and incremental nature of PM²-Agile and support releasing working solutions at regular intervals.
fields.pollux: Same pipeline for all four releases; nothing bespoke per release except the smoke-test list.

fields.what: Setting up a CD pipeline as part of a DevSecOps initiative is a strategic decision described and validated in the plan.
fields.pollux: Pipeline decision recorded at RfE; it removed the manual package hand-off CASTOR needed.

fields.what: DevSecOps brings both ecosystems together; if the organisation is siloed, IT Operations must be integrally involved.
fields.pollux: Operations sits in Release Planning once per release — da Vinci's division supplies the representative.

fields.what: If the Handbook foresees incremental development, the Deployment Plan must foresee a strategy enabling it.
fields.pollux: Both name the pipeline and the same pre-production environment.

fields.what: Deployment efforts are planned with respect to the Release Plan — critical when a separate operations department owns production.
fields.pollux: Cut-over dates derive from the four release dates, never the other way round.

fields.what: Operations must deploy, operate and manage the solution in pre-production; perform several dry-runs before production.
fields.pollux: Two dry-runs before Release 1; one before every later release.

fields.what: Revisited as the project evolves and feedback from previous deployment efforts is gathered.
fields.pollux: Updated after Release 1's cut-over overran by forty minutes on the configuration step.

fields.what: BM I · PM A · TeCo R · PrOw S · ArOw S · ATeM S, plus a contributing representative of the operational unit.
fields.pollux: Lovelace writes it with operations; Hopper is informed of the cut-over windows.

traps: Deployment Plan is technical; Transition Plan and Business Implementation Plan cover people.
TeCo is Responsible, even though it is the most operational artefact.
It has three named sections — deploy, validate, monitor. Learn the three.
Operational Model describes the infrastructure; the Deployment Plan puts software onto it.
It adds a participant no other artefact has: the operational unit representative.
